Find the solution to the initial value problem above.

*Hint: ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14150255/assets/e43485cd9eaca81dd04089924a83a909594e575d76d195850cf11719809acbbd.svg) where ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14150255/assets/6ac1e35cee6cfbab9771278c3a68f422e5422ef79e4f516755e35748ea402e08.svg)*

Writing our system in matrix form, we get
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14150255/assets/b434d5c8a601c3d7fae734a5b78437457fab7877fe0ca1ff466197817d9d1c0e.svg)
where ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14150255/assets/cc9313ae17390c751e51673c53d788c24308f501fa7107e3098cd370028eb1d2.svg) So, the matrix of the system is ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14150255/assets/1d3df45727a13bfbc41ab2689fd1a9a6dbcc28fd4ed071a430a2e745e99aeec8.svg)

Given the system $\mathbf{x}'(t) = A \mathbf{x}(t),$ where $A$ is a constant square matrix, the solution of the initial value problem can be written as

$$
\mathbf{x}(t) = \Phi_0(t) \, \mathbf{x}(0),
$$

where $\Phi_0(t) = e^{At}$ is the standard fundamental matrix of the system, and $\mathbf{x}(0)$ is the initial condition vector.

Now, using the given information, the standard fundamental matrix $\Phi_0(t)$ of the system is given by

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14150255/assets/a998751dcfc2e8acb4e142c5b4a5241ec61fe3bc087dccf9fe87344d73b04ce3.svg)

Therefore, the solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={e}^{At}\,x(0) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t) & \operatorname{sin}⁡(3t) \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t) & \operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t) \\ -2\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)-\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
